query:
Find applicable evidence-backed ways to reduce execution time in this GitHub Actions workflow. Consider its jobs, dependencies, commands, triggers, and repository manifests.
name: Unit tests
on:
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:
# A new push to a pull request cancels the run for the previous commit.
concurrency:
  group: unit-tests-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  unitTests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-26.04
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      # The tests do not need the git history. Without a tag the version is 0.0.0.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: 'jetbrains'
          java-version: '21'
          cache: 'gradle'
      # `--continue` runs all modules even if one fails.
      - name: Run unit tests
        shell: bash
        run: ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest --continue --stacktrace
      - name: Upload test reports
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: test-reports
          path: '**/build/reports/tests/'
          if-no-files-found: ignore

results.content:
Cancel superseded runs

Pattern: P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE (stale_run_cancellation)

When is cancel superseded runs applicable?

Assess cancel superseded runs for this repository, preserve its required checks, and propose a minimal change or NO_CHANGE.

Preconditions: Runs represent the same workflow and branch or PR; A newer revision supersedes older checks

Contraindications: Release or deployment work; Distinct branches share a cancellation group

Method: Partition cancellation by workflow and branch/PR; Preserve run identity and audit records

Reported finding: Superseding runs can reduce duplicate work.

Reported metrics: {"vm_time_reduction_percent": {"free": 1.9, "paid": 4.1}}

Source: Resource Usage and Optimization Opportunities in Workflows of GitHub Actions (2024), 4.2.3; Table 4; PDF pp. 7: https://software-lab.org/publications/icse2024_workflows.pdf

Literature example before:

# ANALYST ILLUSTRATION; NOT PAPER CODE; NOT EXECUTED
finish every revision's CI run


Literature example after:

# ANALYST ILLUSTRATION; NOT PAPER CODE; NOT EXECUTED
cancel an older run only when a newer run supersedes it


Literature example diff:

--- knowledge/examples/P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE/before.txt
+++ knowledge/examples/P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE/after.txt
@@ -1,2 +1,2 @@
 # ANALYST ILLUSTRATION; NOT PAPER CODE; NOT EXECUTED
-finish every revision's CI run
+cancel an older run only when a newer run supersedes it
contraindications: Distinct branches share a cancellation group
preconditions: Runs represent the same workflow and branch or PR

results.content:
Suppress schedules during repository inactivity

Pattern: P-LIT-IDLE-SCHEDULE (scheduled_run_reduction)

When is suppress schedules during repository inactivity applicable?

Assess suppress schedules during repository inactivity for this repository, preserve its required checks, and propose a minimal change or NO_CHANGE.

Preconditions: Periodic results depend only on repository changes

Contraindications: External dependencies, security or time-based requirements need fresh checks

Method: Identify meaningful activity rather than generated self-updates; Resume when relevant inputs change

Reported finding: Inactivity suppression saves some scheduled work.

Reported metrics: {"paid_scheduled_vm_time_reduction_percent": 1.1}

Source: Resource Usage and Optimization Opportunities in Workflows of GitHub Actions (2024), 4.3.2; Table 5; PDF pp. 8, 9: https://software-lab.org/publications/icse2024_workflows.pdf

Literature example before:

# ANALYST ILLUSTRATION; NOT PAPER CODE; NOT EXECUTED
run on every schedule tick


Literature example after:

# ANALYST ILLUSTRATION; NOT PAPER CODE; NOT EXECUTED
run on a tick only if relevant activity occurred
